feedback: Approved to race. This candidate changes one variable from the best raced design, iteration 7 (score 687.1): sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 m, and everything else is held (sensor y 0.08, x spacing +/-0.03, kp 3.8, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.3, line_loss last_direction, weights). The design is valid. All sensor positions are inside the contract limits, 0.016 is an allowed size, and the 16 mm footprints at 15 mm spacing overlap with no gaps. Iteration 6 showed that lateral coverage changes trade slalom line loss against progress (line_loss 1.4 to 1.0, progress 0.46 to 0.31), so this test changes footprint size and leaves lateral spacing alone. Iteration 5 showed that kp 4.0 no longer helps the slalom (progress 0.46 to 0.44), so gain is not the lever. Iteration 4 showed that kd 0.8 helps the s-bend but cuts slalom progress, so kd is not a slalom lever either. Iteration 2 showed that base_speed 1.2 costs more than it gains. The race will show whether a larger footprint reduces slalom edge line loss without hurting the oval or s-bend. Read the result against iteration 7 per track: slalom line_loss_events, max_error and progress; oval finish count; and s-bend steering_oscillation (iteration 7: 0.30).
requested_changes: After the race: if slalom progress rises above 0.46 and slalom line_loss_events fall toward 1.0 or below while the oval stays at 19/20 or better, keep sensor_size 0.016 as the new baseline. Keep kp 3.8, kd 0.8 and base_speed 1.3, because the slalom has not responded to kp or kd changes.

After the race: if the oval drops to 18/20 or below, s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.37, or the score falls below 687, revert to the iteration 7 design exactly (sensor_size 0.012, y 0.08, kp 3.8, kd 0.8, score 687.1). Do not adjust gains to rescue it.

After the race: if the result is neutral (within about 5 points of 687) with the oval intact, test line_loss 'search_left' or 'search_right' only if the slalom telemetry shows a consistent one-sided exit. Keep ki at 0 and base_speed at 1.3.
